audit.why: Akali at 1, Sett from 3 through first item, Akali back at two items matches 49.41% Emerald+ over 3136 games and both on-disk charts. Charts untouched.

audit.whatIsWrong: full breakdown.early was generic template text ('the first levels are about banking small advantages') that contradicts its own chart, which gives Akali level 1 outright; breakdown.spikes read 'Haymaker online, level 6, first item' with no numbers and gave Akali 'levels 2-3'.
audit.why: Level 1 is genuinely Akali's - a dash-less Sett with no Grit stored has nothing to punch back with, which the content layer already says. His actual flip point is Facebreaker at 3, and his level-6 spike is The Show Stopper on 120/100/80s. Twilight Shroud is not learnable before level 3.
audit.corrected: breakdown.early and breakdown.spikes rebuilt on level 1 being yours, Facebreaker at 3, and the 120s ultimate.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer describes Haymaker only as 'Shield + true damage. Shroud it.' — it never says where the shield comes from.
audit.why: Haymaker passively stores the damage Sett TAKES as Grit and spends all of it on cast. Against an energy-gated poke assassin that is the whole matchup: every kunai you land that does not convert into a kill is charging the shield that survives your all-in, and the centre of the punch is true damage so magic resist does nothing about the return. 'Shroud it' does not tell the player that poking him is how he gets paid.
audit.corrected: tldr, report[0].t, winCon, report[1].t, enemyWin, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, dontsFull[1].d and report[11].t now state that your own chip becomes his shield, plus the true-damage centre.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appeared anywhere in the full layer despite every line telling you to 'track Haymaker'.
audit.why: Haymaker 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s, Facebreaker 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s from 490 range, Knuckle Down 9/8/7/6/5s, The Show Stopper 120/100/80s. The content layer already carries the 16s and 9s; the full layer carried nothing.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, winCon, report[1].t and report[9].t now carry them.

audit.whatIsWrong: content wants.foe[2] calls his ultimate 'R (The Show)' and describes it as a suppress.
audit.why: The ability is The Show Stopper, and Riot's text describes a carry-and-slam with a landing slow — it does not use the word suppress, and a half-name reads as a typo on a page whose whole value is naming things correctly.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[2] now uses the full name and drops the unverified suppress wording.
